samples.question: This page shows one solid dark shelf that stretches from near the left edge of the page to near the right edge, together with coloured marks in red, blue, orange, grey, purple and green. Only the dark ink decides the answer; coloured marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured mark is drawn as a ring or sits inside a white basin. Dark ink is a solid wall that water cannot cross. White basins are cut into the shelf, and one straight white channel runs from the top or bottom rim of the shelf towards each basin. Some channels break all the way through into their basin, so that basin is joined to the open water outside the shelf; the other channels stop short behind a wall of dark ink, so that basin is a sealed lagoon. A basin is a sealed lagoon exactly when no white path leads from inside it to the edge of the page without crossing dark ink, and a basin whose channel breaks through is never a sealed lagoon however wide, tall or deep the basin is. A page side is decided by the middle of the page: a basin belongs to the left side if it sits nearer the left edge of the page than the right edge, and to the right side otherwise. Each page side holds the same number of basins and the same number of channels, and the two sides carry nearly the same amount of dark ink, so how many basins there are, how large they are, how much ink each side holds, how many channels reach a rim, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. The two sides never hold equally many sealed lagoons. Which page side holds more sealed lagoons, the left side or the right side? Answer left or right.
